title: Reconcile background job metering attribution when service-account impersonation occurs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Intermittent misattribution of multi-tenant usage for long-running background ingestion jobs that run under service-account impersonation. When short-lived impersonation tokens are rotated or the fronting API key is replaced, downstream metering records sometimes lose the original 'requestor' context and are attributed to the fallback proxy/service account rather than the originating project. This causes retroactive spikes on the proxy account and undercharging for the true customer project.

Observed behavior:
- Batch ingestion job A (customer project P) calls our ingestion endpoint via a service mesh proxy using impersonation headers (X-Impersonate-Actor / token exchange).
- Proxy rotates underlying short-lived token mid-job (automated rotation or sidecar restart).
- Metering pipeline receives usage events with missing/normalized principal_claims and attributes tokens to the proxy service account or tenant-less bucket.
- Billing reports show sudden negative adjustment on project P and matching spike on proxy account during reconciliation windows.

Root cause hypothesis: The metering enrichment layer relies on the inbound api_key metadata or top-level principal claim when constructing attribution. For impersonation flows we normally write an impersonation_chain attribute; however, when token rotation occurs asynchronously the enrichment job processes partial claim sets and overwrites attribution with the active service account. Race between token rotation and event enrichment + our normalization step that favors 'auth_owner' when it exists leads to fallback attribution.

Why this is high priority: Affected customers experience incorrect invoices and quota enforcement gaps. On-call has seen two incidents in the past quarter where retroactive re-billing was requested by finance and caused manual reconciliations. The issue spans Dedicated and Private deployments where customers run their own proxies and use impersonation for cross-project jobs.
proposed_fix:
Design: 1) Extend event schema to persist an ordered impersonation_chain (actor principals + api_key id + timestamp) at ingest time so later stages can deterministically pick the original requestor. 2) Update enrichment pipeline to prefer first_non_service_account principal in the chain for billing attribution. 3) Add idempotent reconciliation logic in billing writer to detect and correct retroactive attributions if chain indicates original project but stored billing_owner differs. 4) Add guard in rate limiter attribution to use effective_owner from chain rather than current token owner when a chain exists.

Implementation notes: small DB migration to add chain metadata to intermediate event table (append-only), resiliency to partial chains, and a safe fallback to existing behavior if chain absent. Changes require coordination with auth/token-service (ENG-589101) to guarantee chain fields are emitted on token exchange.
acceptance_criteria: Ingested events include impersonation_chain when client uses service-account impersonation or token exchange
Billing pipeline attributes >99.9% of background-job token usage to the original project in simulated token-rotation tests
No increase in pipeline tail latency beyond 5% under load test suite
Automated reconciliation run corrects previously misattributed events in a staging snapshot and produces consistent audit logs
E2E QA with a dedicated test project demonstrates correct invoice-level aggregation for a 24h rotation window
test_plan: Unit tests for chain encoding/decoding, integration tests between auth service and ingest (stubbed exchange), load test injecting token-rotation mid-stream and verifying attribution, and a retrospective reconciliation dry-run against a 7-day window of historical events in staging. QA steps documented in the linked test playbook. Mock customers: proj-test-impersonation-1 and proj-test-impersonation-2.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the enrichment changes behind 'impersonation_chain_enrich'. 2) Deploy ingestion + enrichment update to staging and run full test_plan. 3) Canary deploy to production region us-west-2 on low traffic weekend with reconciliation off by default. 4) Gradually enable reconciliation for up-to-2h windows on canary region and monitor billing diffs. 5) Full rollout and schedule background reconciliation run to correct historical drift. 6) Post-rollout audit and customer communication for any affected accounts.
monitoring: New metric: attribution_mismatch_rate (events where billing_owner != first_non_service_account_in_chain)
Alert: attribution_mismatch_rate > 0.1% for 10m -> SEV-2 paging to billing oncall
Dashboard: per-project delta between ingested_token_owner and effective_owner over time
Reconciliation job health: success/failure counts and corrected_event_count
